As get_current_working_dir() currently returns a cached value I do not expect this to work as expected unfortunately: we should also update the cached value current_working_dir so that the next call to ws_pushd() works fine.
I guess it works fine in the context of the Diameter dissector simply because you call ws_popd() before another call to ws_pushd().

changed this line in [version 6 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20197/diffs?diff_id=1390712426&start_sha=0104ba87dc4b93ec8eb42a41e827f659da38c2b0#3a9191283cda933433cbff7b074876dd674f96b6_207_207)

Unsure of the intended use of these functions besides something similar to Diameter dissector (that needs to "force" a simple relative path to load some files and then it's done).  It's good that glib has a platform independent implementation for getting the current directory, so I just changed the patch to use it directly and not the cached value from current_working_dir.

Given the comments found in get_current_working_dir(), calling g_get_current_dir() during runtime might not be a good idea. Given that we already know what is the initial working dir and that we are gonna set it ourselves, using get_current_working_dir() and updating the cached value seems a better idea.

Easy enough to revert, but is having these functions to begin with a good idea?  Again, I don't see much use case besides Diameter dissector (!20074), potentially other clients of libxml2 (that use external entities) and possibly libsmi (#1827).

If there is more than 1 dissector needing this function, it makes sense to have the code factorized somehow. But maybe the push/pop queue is overkill for now and we should only allow a single call at a time. We could even turn them into macros and save the current working directory in the context of the dissector (the macros would be hiding the windows vs linux/mac differences).

I'm fine for "overkill", but I did like the suggestion of combining this functionality into 1 wsutil function (not macro).  The push/pop remain, but hidden behind the new ws_execute_in_directory function.

Are there any cases where more than one thread might try to change the current directory out from under another thread?

POSIX doesn't have a 'pthread_chdir()` call; Darwin appears to have an undocumented `__phread_chdir()` system call, but I don't know what other UN\*Xes, if any, have it. Windows also doesn't appear to have per-thread current directories.

I was trying to make this generic, but does it make sense to put this API in epan to imply it's only used by dissectors (during the "single thread" of initializing them).  That's at least the only current use case.

> Windows also doesn't appear to have per-thread current directories.

Indeed, per
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-getcurrentdirectory

"Multithreaded applications and shared library code should not use the GetCurrentDirectory function and should avoid using relative path names. The current directory state written by the SetCurrentDirectory function is stored as a global variable in each process, therefore multithreaded applications cannot reliably use this value without possible data corruption from other threads that may also be reading or setting this value. This limitation also applies to the SetCurrentDirectory and GetFullPathName functions."
Ended up moving the functionality to epan (and hopefully made the comments clear) of the functions intended purpose (which at the moment is just the diameter dissector)

changes_data.diff:
@@ -1108,6 +1108,21 @@ void proto_init(GSList *register_all_plugin_protocols_list,
 /** Frees memory used by proto routines. Called at program shutdown */
 extern void proto_cleanup(void);
 
+typedef void (*proto_execute_in_directory_func)(void* param);
+
+/** Execute a function for a protocol in a specific directory.
+ * This will change the current working directory, then execute
+ * the function and then restore the current working directory to
+ * its previous value.  This is intended to be called during protocol
+ * initialization (i.e. not thread safe)
+ *
+ * @param dir The new current working directory
+ * @param func Function to be called once the directory has been successfully changed
+ * @param param Optional parameter to be passed into the handling function
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC void proto_execute_in_directory(const char* dir, proto_execute_in_directory_func func, void* param);
+
+
 /** This function takes a tree and a protocol id as parameter and
